semantics: For each target group: 'levels' is the ordered hierarchy from broadest to the observation unit; a dimension left out is not a borrowing dimension for that group (for example treatment for baseline sex). 'tau_prior_scale' is the half-normal prior scale of the between-sibling standard deviation at that level, on the analysis scale (logit for proportions, log for ratios, years for age). A large scale says siblings may differ a lot (the dimension matters, borrowing is weak); a small scale says they are expected to be similar (strong borrowing). Every tau is then estimated from the data; the prior only matters where evidence is sparse.
